§6Naphtha§f

§aCrack it, reform it, or fraction it down. This mid-weight fraction has options.§f

Naphtha is the second most common refinery output at §e250mB§f per §e1,000mB§f hot crude oil. Medium fuel value (§e110 kTU§f / §e165 kHE§f per bucket) with several processing routes.

§6Fractioning Tower§f:
§e100mB§f Naphtha → §e60mB§f Diesel + §e40mB§f Heating Oil.

§6Catalytic Reformer§f:
§e1,000mB§f Naphtha → §e500mB§f Reformate + §e150mB§f Petroleum Gas + §e100mB§f Liquid Hydrogen.

§6Chemical Plant§f:
§e1,000mB§f Naphtha → §e800mB§f Gasoline.

§6Other Uses§f:
§b• Industrial Mixer§f: §e500mB§f Naphtha + §e500mB§f Aromatic Hydrocarbons → §e1,000mB§f §bSolvent§f.
§b• Coker Unit§f: §e4,900mB§f → §e1× Petroleum Coke§f.
§b• Pyrolysis Oven§f: §e6,500mB§f → §e1× Solid Fuel§f.
§b• Solidification§f: §e16,000mB§f → §e1× Solid Fuel§f.

§ePS:§f Naphtha's fuel value is higher than Heavy Oil. Fraction it to §bDiesel§f for best fuel efficiency, or reform it for higher-value products.
